copy.title: The Messi Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Lionel Messi’s family: the father who ran his business, the Inter Miami deal, the tax case, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #032 · The Messi family · Data as of
copy.h1: Football’s other billionaire has a family. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what he owns, what the clubs paid him, which companies you can buy stock in, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file. Lionel and Antonela’s three sons appear by first name only.
copy.investLede: His clubs and businesses are private. Adidas, which pays him under a lifetime deal, trades in Frankfurt, but the family has no stake in it.
copy.moneyLede: Mostly cash saved from two decades of contracts and endorsements, plus an option to own part of Inter Miami. Only Lionel has a published net worth.
copy.recordLede: What leaked contracts, the players’ union and a Spanish court record show. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From Rosario to Barcelona at 13, and to a billion dollars at 38.
copy.calcYearsK: Years to earn what Lionel has

summary.t: Worked as a department head at a steel plant before becoming his son’s agent and business manager. He negotiated the Barcelona contracts and the moves to Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami, and handled the family’s real estate, hotel and restaurant investments. He died on Aug. 8, 2026, at 68.

record.t: In 2016 a Spanish court sentenced him and Lionel to 21 months each for tax fraud over endorsement income sheltered from Spanish taxes. The jail terms were expected to be suspended. He was fined €1.5 million.

summary.t: Worked in a magnet manufacturing workshop in Rosario while raising four children: Rodrigo, Matías, Lionel and María Sol.

Played 17 years for FC Barcelona and two for Paris Saint-Germain before joining Inter Miami in 2023. He led Argentina to the 2022 World Cup and retired from the national team in August 2026 with a record 124 goals.

owns.t: Plays for the club under a contract through 2028, with an option to take an equity stake when he retires.
Holds a stake through Edificio Rostower Socimi, a listed real estate company he launched in 2024.
Cofounded it with Luis Suárez in 2025.
Bought it in April 2026 for an undisclosed price.

record.t: Forbes estimates about $1.2 billion from playing contracts and more than $600 million from endorsements, memorabilia and other business, before taxes and agents’ fees. It first counted him a billionaire in June 2026.
A leaked four-year deal from 2017 showed about $177 million in pay for the 2017-18 season alone.
His guaranteed MLS pay for 2026 is $28.3 million, per the players’ union. Club owner Jorge Mas told Bloomberg Messi is paid $70 million to $80 million a year in all.
In 2016 a Spanish court found him and his father guilty of tax fraud over endorsement income held through shell companies in tax havens. They avoided jail; Lionel was fined about €2 million.

facts.t: He left Nike for Adidas in 2006 and signed a lifetime deal with Adidas in 2017. Its value wasn’t disclosed.
Inter Miami was worth about $600 million before he arrived. Forbes now values it at $1.35 billion, the highest in MLS.
Forbes ranked him No. 3 among the world’s highest-paid athletes in 2026, with $140 million.

kidsNote.t: Lionel and Antonela have three sons: Thiago, Mateo and Ciro. We list first names only.

summary.t: They met as children in Rosario through her cousin, a youth teammate of Lionel’s, and married there in June 2017. She has more than 40 million Instagram followers.
